forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Edges down 1pp. June 2026 AI coverage stresses agents-in-production and 'hype is over'; no credible lab AGI declaration and definitional consensus still absent. Altman's 'we built AGIs' remark remains rhetorical, not a resolving announcement.
forecasts.base_rate: No reference class of a breakthrough technology being universally declared 'general intelligence'. Lab-CEO timelines (2026-2030) have poor calibration history and are upper-bound predictions.

factors_up.factor: Continued agentic capability gains; agents now working in real enterprise systems
Musk and several lab leaders maintain near-term AGI theses

factors_down.factor: No consensus definition of 'AGI achieved'; resolution bar (lab announcement OR 3+ researchers) unmet
Skeptics (LeCun, Stanford HAI's Landay) firm that LLMs alone won't reach AGI; narrative shifting from demos to deployment

key_uncertainties: Definitional threshold for declaring 'AGI'
Whether 3+ leading researchers would jointly state AGI achieved
Lab incentives to declare AGI for commercial/regulatory reasons
update_triggers: Coordinated researcher statement that AGI is achieved
Benchmark saturation across general reasoning suites

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Up 1pp. McKinsey ~10% cuts (3,000-4,000 roles) confirmed and attributed partly to AI; Bain, BCG, Deloitte implementing similar staffing reductions; Forrester cites 40% AI productivity gains compressing the analyst pyramid.
forecasts.base_rate: Past sectoral disruptions (travel agents, paralegals) show ~33% declines over five years are uncommon but occur when productivity gains exceed ~40% and demand does not fully offset.

factors_up.factor: McKinsey cutting ~10% of workforce; managing partner signals further non-client cuts over two years
40% reported AI productivity gains; junior 'pyramid' staffing model under structural pressure across firms

factors_down.factor: Current cuts (~10%) far below 33%; many are back-office, not core advisory revenue
BCG growing headcount via AI/tech specialists; demand for AI-transformation advice partly offsets displacement

key_uncertainties: Whether revenue (not just headcount) declines and is attributed primarily to AI
Demand offset from AI-transformation consulting work
Whether 2+ credible analyses attribute a >=33% fall to AI by 2030
update_triggers: Sector revenue or headcount down >20% with explicit AI attribution
Multiple top firms announce structural >25% reductions
Demand rebound from AI advisory work reverses cuts

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: No change. YouGov 7-8 June puts Reform 25%, Lab 19% (tied with Con); PollCheck average has Reform ~28%, Labour ~19%. Labour trails badly, though the next GE (by 2029) leaves room for recovery and FPTP seat translation is uncertain.
forecasts.base_rate: Governing parties trailing by ~8-9pp mid-term sometimes recover, but a sustained second-place-or-worse position this large rarely converts to most seats; reference class of incumbents recovering from such deficits is thin.

factors_up.factor: ~3.5 years to the election allow substantial mean-reversion
Fragmented vote (Reform, Con, Green) can let Labour win seats on low vote share under FPTP

factors_down.factor: Reform UK holds a clear, sustained lead since mid-2025; Labour down to high-teens
Labour now level with Conservatives, no recovery momentum

key_uncertainties: Timing of the next general election
How Reform's vote share translates into seats under FPTP
Whether Labour can rebuild a governing coalition by 2029

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: No change. The decade horizon remains long enough that most lab and aggregate-survey timelines place AGI before 2035, even allowing for definitional disputes and slower-than-hyped near-term progress.
forecasts.base_rate: Aggregated expert and prediction-market timelines cluster AGI medians in the late 2020s to early 2030s; a 2035 cutoff sits above most central estimates.

factors_up.factor: Sustained compute and capability scaling; agentic systems maturing into deployment
Most lab leaders and survey medians put AGI before 2035

factors_down.factor: Definitional contestation could leave 'AGI' formally undeclared even amid strong capability
Possible scaling/compute or capital constraints before 2035

key_uncertainties: Whether scaling continues to yield general capability through the early 2030s
Agreement on what counts as 'AGI achieved'
Capital and compute availability over the decade
update_triggers: Clear capability plateau across frontier models
Formal AGI declaration by a credible lab

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: No change. AEI and ASPI assessments judge a 2026 blockade/invasion unlikely; Beijing persists with grey-zone coercion. 2027 remains the cited PLA capability milestone, keeping non-trivial tail risk through the end-2029 window.
forecasts.base_rate: Cross-strait kinetic initiation has not occurred in the modern era despite repeated crises; base rate of a major power launching such an assault in any given multi-year window is low.

factors_up.factor: PLA rehearsing blockades and infrastructure strikes (Strait Thunder, Justice Mission exercises)
2027 capability milestone falls inside the window

factors_down.factor: Analysts assess 2026 invasion/blockade unlikely; Beijing prefers coercion short of kinetic action
High costs and uncertain outcome of a blockade/assault deter initiation

key_uncertainties: Xi's risk tolerance and internal political timeline
Whether grey-zone coercion crosses the >72hr blockade threshold
US/allied deterrence posture through 2029

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Down 1pp. April 2026 CPI came in at 2.8% (down from 3.3% in March) but the ONS/analysts flag the slowdown as short-lived. Only ~7 monthly prints remain before Jan 2027, leaving little room to reach sub-2.0%.
forecasts.base_rate: From a 2.8% reading with an expected near-term re-acceleration, dropping below 2.0% within a handful of months is historically uncommon absent a demand shock.

factors_up.factor: April energy price cap drove a sharp housing-services disinflation; further base effects possible
Several monthly readings still to come before the deadline

factors_down.factor: Latest print 2.8%; slowdown expected to be short-lived per ONS/analyst commentary
Services/core inflation sticky; a sub-2.0% single month would require a sharp, fast decline

key_uncertainties: Energy and food base effects through H2 2026
Persistence of services inflation
Any demand shock that accelerates disinflation
update_triggers: A monthly CPI print at or below ~2.2%

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Up 1pp. Tracking strengthens: record trailer views and a ~55% Polymarket implied probability of finishing 2026 as the top-grossing film. Releases 31 July 2026, giving five months of run before the deadline, but $1.5B remains a rare threshold.
forecasts.base_rate: Only a small number of films have ever grossed >$1.5B; among MCU/Spider-Man entries, No Way Home (~$1.9B) cleared it but most franchise films land well below.

factors_up.factor: Record-setting trailer views and strong pre-release demand signals
Prime summer release with ~5 months of theatrical run before 31 Dec

factors_down.factor: $1.5B is a threshold few films reach; even strong MCU titles often fall short
Trailer views are an imperfect predictor of final gross; China/legs risk

key_uncertainties: Opening weekend magnitude and legs
China and other international performance
Competitive summer/holiday box-office environment
update_triggers: Opening weekend well above No Way Home pace

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Down 1pp for calibration. As of April 2026 OpenAI ~$25B and Anthropic ~$30B ARR (combined ~$55B), both growing rapidly; reaching a combined >$70B by Q4 2026 needs only ~$15B more across ~8 months, highly likely even on conservative reporting.
forecasts.base_rate: Both firms have roughly doubled or more in under a year; extrapolating current run-rate growth comfortably clears the threshold within the window.

factors_up.factor: Combined ARR already ~$55B in April 2026 with steep growth trajectories
Enterprise demand (esp. Anthropic) and OpenAI monetisation both expanding fast

factors_down.factor: Accounting dispute (gross vs net) could shave Anthropic's reported figure by ~$8B
Possible growth deceleration or reporting timing around Q4 2026

key_uncertainties: Which ARR definition credible outlets report for Q4 2026
Whether growth holds through H2 2026
Timing/availability of Q4 2026 figures
update_triggers: Credible Q4 2026 ARR reporting below ~$65B combined
Standardisation on a stricter net ARR definition

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Down 2pp. OBR March 2026 has real GDP averaging ~1.5% over the forecast and GDP-per-person just ~1.1% to 2030, with productivity revised down and labour-supply growth falling toward 0.5% by 2030 on ageing and lower migration - making a >1.5% decade average a coin-flip-or-worse.
forecasts.base_rate: UK decade-average real GDP growth has trended down across recent decades; exceeding 1.5% requires either a productivity rebound or stronger labour-supply growth than currently projected.

factors_up.factor: OBR/2018 FSR long-run assumption of productivity rising toward ~2% from 2030-31
AI projected to add ~0.2pp to annual productivity by the horizon

factors_down.factor: Productivity forecasts revised down; near-term GDP-per-person only ~1.1%
Labour-supply growth falling toward ~0.5% by 2030 (ageing, lower net migration)

key_uncertainties: Whether the assumed productivity pick-up materialises
Net migration and labour-force participation paths
Scale and timing of AI's productivity contribution
update_triggers: Further downward productivity or migration revisions
